incident.title: Checkout connection pool exhaustion triggers retry storm
incident.summary: A slow query held a database connection past its expected duration, saturating checkout-service's connection pool. New requests queued indefinitely with no timeout, and upstream clients began retrying aggressively, amplifying load until the service became unresponsive.

trigger.description: checkout-service's database connection pool reached its configured maximum size and began queuing new connection requests indefinitely.
preconditions: fixed-size connection pool with no acquisition timeout
a slow query can hold a connection far longer than the typical case

events.description: A single query against checkout-db begins holding its connection well past normal duration.
The connection pool reaches its configured maximum size as concurrent request volume continues arriving.
New requests queue for a connection with no acquisition timeout, backing up the request handler.
Upstream clients time out waiting on queued requests and begin retrying, further increasing load on the saturated pool.

side_effects.description: Widespread request timeouts across dependent services as queued requests exceed client-side deadlines.

business_invariants.statement: A request must either complete or fail within a bounded time; it must never queue indefinitely.

expected_corrected_behavior:
Connection acquisition from the pool must have a bounded timeout, and a request that cannot acquire a connection within that timeout must fail fast rather than queue indefinitely.
Client retries must use bounded exponential backoff with jitter so a saturated dependency is not amplified by a retry storm.

reproduction_sequence.description: Issue a query against checkout-db that holds its connection well past normal duration.
Generate enough concurrent request volume to saturate the remaining pool capacity.
Observe requests queuing with no bound and clients beginning to retry.

privacy.notes: Contains only synthetic identifiers and a fictional scenario; no real customer, payment, or credential data is present.
